research_notes: Research for France Travel Scams book. Colmar is notably safer than major French cities (ranked #5 safest in France for solo travelers, 4.5/5 safety rating). The main concerns are train station organized theft, Christmas market pickpocketing, and restaurant overcharging in tourist areas. Sources include UK FCDO, US Embassy France, TripAdvisor, Rick Steves, Connexion France.

scams.location: Colmar train station (Gare de Colmar), platform stairs, luggage areas
scams.story: Organized groups of thieves operate at Colmar train station, posing as helpful strangers offering to assist tourists with their luggage. Two or three young individuals approach travelers on stairs or near platforms, insisting on helping carry bags despite refusals. While one person distracts with conversation or blocks your view, another rifles through bags or pockets, stealing passports, wallets, and valuables.
red_flags: Strangers persistently offering to help with luggage despite being declined
Multiple people approaching simultaneously
One person creating distraction while others position behind you
Helpers following you to your train carriage after initial refusal
how_to_avoid: Firmly decline all unsolicited help with luggage
Ask station staff in red tabards for assistance if needed
Keep bags zipped and secured in front of your body
Travel with only luggage you can manage alone

scams.location: Colmar Christmas Markets, Place des Dominicains, Place de l'Ancienne Douane, Petite Venise, medieval Old Town pedestrian streets
scams.story: During Colmar's famous Christmas markets (late November through December), professional pickpockets work the dense crowds moving between market stalls. Victims often report having wallets stolen from zipped crossbody purses or coat pockets while navigating the narrow medieval streets packed with holiday shoppers. The crush of tourists photographing half-timbered houses creates perfect cover for skilled thieves.
red_flags: Strangers bumping into you repeatedly in crowd
Someone creating a distraction while an accomplice reaches for your bag
Overly friendly people engaging you in conversation in crowded areas
People standing unusually close in less-crowded spots
how_to_avoid: Wear crossbody bags in front of your body with locking zippers
Keep wallets in front pockets or money belts under clothing
Visit markets Monday-Thursday when crowds are lighter
Avoid peak weekend hours between 11am-5pm

scams.location: Little Venice (Petite Venise), Place de l'Ancienne Douane, Rue des Marchands, areas near Maison Pfister
scams.story: Certain restaurants in Colmar's heavily-touristed areas engage in deceptive pricing practices. Visitors have reported being charged 7 euros extra per person when attempting to share a menu. Other tactics include presenting tourists with different menus featuring inflated prices, adding undisclosed charges for bread or water, or bringing unrequested items and billing for them.
red_flags: No prices displayed outside the restaurant
Staff steering you to 'special' tourist menus
Verbal price quotes that differ from written menus
Menus only available in English with no French version
how_to_avoid: Check prices on posted menus before sitting down
Eat where locals eat - venture a few streets from main tourist paths
Review recent TripAdvisor and Google reviews before dining
Ask for itemized bill and verify all charges match menu prices

scams.location: Colmar train station area, Place Rapp, near Musee Unterlinden, Cathedral of Saint Martin, tourist walking areas
scams.story: Groups of individuals approach tourists with clipboards, asking them to sign petitions for fake charitable causes, often pretending to be deaf-mute. The petitions are typically in English (suspicious in a French city) and claim to support disabled people. After signing, they reveal a 'donation' column and pressure you for 10-20 euros. While you're distracted, an accomplice may be pickpocketing you.
red_flags: Groups of young people with identical clipboards
Claims of supporting deaf/mute charities
Petition written primarily in English
Requests for cash donations immediately after signing
how_to_avoid: Say 'Non, merci' firmly and keep walking without stopping
Never sign anything offered by strangers on the street
Keep your bag secured in front of you if approached
Remember that legitimate charities don't solicit cash on streets

scams.location: Standalone ATMs in tourist areas, train station ATMs, ATMs on Rue des Marchands, machines near Christmas markets
scams.story: France experiences 42% of all European bank card fraud. Criminals install skimming devices on ATMs that capture card data and hidden cameras or keypad overlays that record PIN entries. Tourist areas are prime targets because foreign cards are less likely to have advanced security features. Victims typically discover the theft weeks later when unauthorized charges appear on their statements.
red_flags: ATM card slot that looks loose, crooked, or different from other machines
Unusual attachments or bulkiness around the keypad
Scratches or adhesive residue around the card slot
Machine that 'eats' your card without returning it
how_to_avoid: Use ATMs inside banks during business hours only
Inspect the card slot and keypad before inserting card - wiggle the slot
Always cover your hand when entering PIN
Set up transaction alerts on your cards before traveling

scams.location: Colmar train station, parking areas near Old Town, near tourist attractions, quiet side streets
scams.story: Scammers pose as plainclothes police officers, quickly flashing fake badges and demanding to 'check your documents and wallet for counterfeit currency.' While examining your wallet, they palm cash or memorize card details. Some wear partial uniforms or hats with police markings to appear legitimate. French authorities have warned about increased incidents of criminals impersonating officers.
red_flags: Officers demanding to see your wallet, phone, or cash (real police only ask for ID)
Badge flashed too quickly to read or examine
No uniform or inconsistent uniform elements
Refusal to provide their serial number when asked
how_to_avoid: Know that real French police will NEVER demand your wallet, cash, or phone
Ask to see proper identification and request their serial number
Suggest going to the nearest police station together for any document checks
Call 17 (police emergency) if unsure about legitimacy

scams.location: Public parking meters throughout Colmar, parking areas near Old Town, tourist parking zones
scams.story: Scammers place fake QR code stickers over legitimate ones on parking meters throughout France. When tourists scan the fraudulent code, they're directed to a convincing phishing website that mimics official parking payment services. Victims enter their license plate, parking duration, and credit card details - all captured by criminals. Some victims are tricked into entering multiple card numbers after being told their payment 'failed.'
red_flags: QR code appears to be a sticker placed over another code
Website URL doesn't match official city parking services
Payment site asks for excessive personal information
Multiple payment 'failures' requesting different cards
how_to_avoid: Run your finger over QR codes to detect if it's a sticker covering another code
Type parking payment URLs directly rather than scanning codes
Use official parking apps downloaded from app stores, not QR links
Pay at meter using coin or chip-enabled card rather than QR when possible

scams.location: Alsace Wine Route villages (Eguisheim, Riquewihr, Kaysersberg), small caves in Colmar, roadside tasting rooms
scams.story: While wine tastings along the Alsace Wine Route often appear free, there's strong social pressure to purchase bottles afterward. Some establishments serve generous pours to lower inhibitions, create false scarcity ('last bottles of this vintage'), or make tourists feel obligated after extensive tastings. Staff may become noticeably cold or hostile if visitors don't make purchases.
red_flags: No posted prices visible before tasting begins
Pressure to buy immediately 'before stock runs out'
Tasting fees not disclosed upfront that appear on bill afterward
Staff attitude changing dramatically if you don't purchase
how_to_avoid: Look for 'Vignobles et Decouvertes' certified wineries for quality assurance
Set a budget before entering any cave and stick to it
Know it's perfectly acceptable to taste and buy just one bottle or none at all
Ask about tasting fees upfront before sampling begins

scams.location: Tourist parking areas along Wine Route, parking lots at village viewpoints, free parking zones near attractions, trailhead parking
scams.story: Thieves specifically target rental cars parked at tourist attractions throughout Alsace. They watch parking lots for tourists who open their trunks to store or retrieve items, marking which vehicles contain valuables. Rental cars are easily identified by registration stickers, missing floor mats, and clean interiors. Travelers return from wine tastings to find windows smashed and all belongings stolen.
red_flags: Free parking areas at popular tourist sites
Parking lots without security cameras or attendants
Strangers appearing to loiter or watch parked cars
Parking areas with broken glass on the ground
how_to_avoid: Never open your trunk in the parking lot where thieves might see contents
Retrieve needed items a mile before arriving at destination
Remove all visible items including guidebooks, maps, and ticket stubs
Use underground or multistorey car parks with CCTV when possible

scams.location: Online platforms, fake booking websites, phishing emails
scams.story: Scammers create fake listings mimicking real Colmar properties on platforms like Airbnb and Booking.com, or send phishing emails claiming your reservation was cancelled with large penalty charges. Colmar's picturesque half-timbered houses make it easy to steal photos for convincing fake listings. Victims arrive to find their 'charming Alsatian apartment' doesn't exist.
red_flags: Prices significantly below market rate for Colmar Old Town properties
Host pressuring you to pay outside the official platform
Emails about cancellations asking you to click links or call unfamiliar numbers
No reviews or only very recent positive reviews
how_to_avoid: Book only through official platforms and pay within their secure system
Verify emails by logging into booking sites directly, never via email links
Cross-reference property photos using reverse image search
Read reviews carefully and look for specific details about Colmar location
